course_profile.one_sentence_summary: An introductory bachelor-level course covering software lifecycles, reverse engineering, software metrics, cost estimation, and process maturity models.
course_profile.short_summary: This course provides foundational knowledge in software engineering, distinguishing between direct, reverse, and empirical engineering. Students learn to model software development lifecycles (including Agile methodologies), estimate software costs using models like COCOMO and SLIM, calculate software metrics, and evaluate software ecosystems and process maturity (CMM/CMMI).

theoretical_understanding: Understand the historical context and foundational concepts of software engineering.
Comprehend different software development lifecycle models and process maturity frameworks like CMMI.
Understand the core principles of software economics and cost estimation models (COCOMO, SLIM).
Understand the definition and utility of software ecosystems.
practical_implementation: Model software development lifecycles, including sequential and agile methodologies.
Perform reverse engineering to extract component information from existing software systems.
Calculate and analyze empirical software metrics.
analysis_validation: Analyze the economic indicators and cost associated with creating and maintaining software.
Evaluate software architectures and components using both forward and reverse engineering techniques.
architecture_design: Model requirements specification, architecture, detailed design, construction, and maintenance processes.
research_and_prototyping: Investigate legacy systems using reverse engineering tools to comprehend undocumented structures.

expected_artifacts: Software cost estimations based on COCOMO/SLIM
implementation_tasks: Model software architecture and detailed design phases.
Model software construction and testing processes.
Apply reverse engineering to analyze software components.
Evaluate software costs using standard economic models.

curricular_relations.reason: Understanding object-oriented code is a necessary prerequisite to successfully reverse engineer and extract software components.
General SDLC modeling fundamentals serve as the basis before modeling specific agile processes.
Software size and complexity metrics are often inputs for cost estimation models like COCOMO.

what_student_can_understand: The stages and processes involved in the software development lifecycle.
How software process maturity is measured using CMMI.
The theoretical foundations of forward, reverse, and empirical software engineering.
what_student_can_build: Process models representing requirements, design, and construction phases.
Software cost estimates using industry-standard algorithmic models.
what_student_can_apply: Reverse engineering techniques to analyze existing programs.
COCOMO and SLIM methods to predict software project costs and effort.
i* framework to model software ecosystems.
